title: Drug Testing Software: Workplace Programs and Lab Workflows
summary: Learn what drug testing software does for workplace programs and testing labs: random selection, DOT compliance, chain of custody and audit-ready reporting.

- Drug testing software manages drug and alcohol tests from order to final record.
- Employers and TPAs use program software for random selection, orders and compliance reports.
- Testing labs need lab software for accessioning, chain of custody, results, QC and review.
- For DOT tests, 49 CFR Part 40 sets the rules for labs, records and record retention.

Drug testing protects safety-sensitive work. Many teams still use spreadsheets, paper forms and email to run it. These tools cause entry errors and lost records. Drug testing software replaces them with one controlled system.


But "drug testing software" means two kinds of tools. Employers and third-party administrators (TPAs) use program software. Testing labs use lab software. This guide explains both. It also shows what DOT rules ask for and how to select a system.


## What is drug testing software?


Drug testing software is a digital system that manages drug and alcohol tests. It records each step, from the test order to the final result. It also keeps the records that audits need.


Most systems give these core features:


- **Test ordering and scheduling.** The system sends the donor to a collection site and tracks the status.
- **Random selection.** The system selects employees from a pool for random tests.
- **Results tracking.** The system shows the status and result of each test.
- **Compliance reporting.** The system makes audit-ready reports and keeps records for the required time.
- **Integrations.** The system connects to HR systems, labs and Medical Review Officers (MROs).


## Workplace drug testing software vs. drug testing lab software


The two tools serve different users. Select the tool that matches your role.


### Workplace program software


- **Main users:** employers, TPAs, HR and safety teams.
- **Main record:** the employee and the test event.
- **Key tasks:** employee pools, random selection, test orders and compliance reports.
- **Typical tools:** drug testing management software.


### Drug testing lab software


- **Main users:** toxicology labs, clinical labs and lab QA teams.
- **Main record:** the specimen and its result.
- **Key tasks:** accessioning, chain of custody, instrument data, QC, review and the final report.
- **Typical tools:** a toxicology LIMS or a lab LIMS.


Employers usually do not run the lab work. A certified lab tests the specimen. The lab then reports the result for MRO review. So the lab needs its own software for the specimen journey.


## How drug testing lab software supports chain of custody and results


A drug test result is only as strong as its record. The lab must show who handled each specimen, when, and what happened to it. Drug testing lab software records these steps.


A typical lab workflow has these steps:


1. **Accessioning.** The lab receives the specimen and gives it a unique ID.[Sample accessioning](https://www.scispot.com/blog/the-importance-of-sample-accessioning-in-improving-lab-efficiency) creates the first controlled record in the chain of custody.
2. **Chain of custody.** The system records each transfer, user and time. This makes the record defensible in an audit.
3. **Testing and instrument data.** The system imports results from instruments. This removes manual re-entry.
4. **QC and review.** The system checks controls and flags out-of-range values. A qualified reviewer approves the result.
5. **Reporting and records.** The system releases the approved result and keeps the full record.


Clinical labs in the U.S. also work under CLIA. The[CMS CLIA program](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/quality/clinical-laboratory-improvement-amendments) sets quality standards so that patient test results are accurate, reliable and timely. ## DOT drug testing compliance: what your software must support


The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) sets drug and alcohol test procedures in[49 CFR Part 40](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/subtitle-A/part-40) . Part 40 applies to transportation employers, safety-sensitive employees and service agents. Your software must help you follow these rules:


- **Certified labs only.** Under[49 CFR 40.81](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/subtitle-A/part-40/subpart-F/section-40.81) , a U.S. lab can do DOT drug testing only if HHS certifies it under the National Laboratory Certification Program (NLCP). The certification applies to each testing method the lab uses.
- **Record retention.** Under[49 CFR 40.333](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/subtitle-A/part-40/subpart-P/section-40.333) , employers keep verified positive drug test results for five years. They keep negative and cancelled drug test results for one year.
- **Controlled access.** The same section says that employers must keep records in a location with controlled access.
- **Usable electronic records.** Electronic records must be easy to access, legible and organized. If they are not, the employer must convert them to printed records when DOT agency staff ask.


For federal workplace programs,[SAMHSA's Drug-Free Workplace Programs](https://www.samhsa.gov/substance-use/drug-free-workplace) page lists resources for labs and testers. These include the certified lab list, the HHS Mandatory Guidelines, the MRO manual and federal custody and control forms.


## How to choose drug testing software


Use these questions to compare systems:


1. **Who is the user?** An employer or TPA needs program software. A testing lab needs lab software. Some teams need both, connected.
2. **Does it keep a full audit trail?** Every change must show the user, the time and the reason.
3. **Does it support e-signatures and approvals?** Reviewers must sign off on results in the system.
4. **Does it connect to your instruments and partners?** Manual file moves cause errors. Ask which instrument types the vendor supports.
5. **Can it scale?** Test volume grows. The system must handle more specimens without more manual work.
6. **Does the vendor support validation?** Regulated labs must validate their systems. Ask what validation support the vendor gives.
